[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient 1: [redacted name] (Female)
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]

Patient 2: [redacted name] (Male)
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]

Ordering Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Carrier testing for Cystic Fibrosis requested for expectant couple. Female patient reports family history of Cystic Fibrosis in cousin. Causative variants in affected cousin are unknown.

TEST PERFORMED
Cystic Fibrosis Carrier Screen
Methodology: GeneScreen-CF50 kit
Gene analyzed: CFTR (NM_000492.4)

METHODOLOGY
Targeted genotyping was performed using the GeneScreen-CF50 kit, which screens for 50 common pathogenic variants in the CFTR gene. This panel detects approximately 88% of disease-causing variants in individuals of Caucasian ancestry, 38% in individuals of South Asian ancestry, and 76% of Cystic Fibrosis causing variants worldwide. The assay utilizes allele-specific PCR amplification followed by capillary electrophoresis for variant detection.

RESULTS

Patient 1 ([redacted name], Female):
CFTR variant screen: NEGATIVE
No pathogenic variants detected among the 50 variants tested

Patient 2 ([redacted name], Male):
CFTR variant screen: NEGATIVE
No pathogenic variants detected among the 50 variants tested

INTERPRETATION
Neither individual was found to carry any of the 50 common CFTR pathogenic variants included in this screening panel. Based on these results:

- The female patient's carrier risk is reduced from the general population risk of ~1/25 to approximately 1/12. This residual risk may differ if the specific familial variants were known.
- The male patient's carrier risk is reduced from ~1/25 to approximately 1/122
- The couple's combined risk of having a child affected with Cystic Fibrosis is approximately 1/5,856

LIMITATIONS
This test screens for 50 common CFTR pathogenic variants and does not detect all possible disease-causing variants in the CFTR gene. Rare or private variants, deep intronic variants, and large deletions/duplications are not detected by this assay. The detection rate varies by ethnicity. Full gene sequencing may be considered if clinical suspicion remains high or if identification of familial variants is desired.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Based on the significantly reduced carrier risk in both partners, prenatal diagnosis for Cystic Fibrosis is NOT indicated for this couple. Genetic counseling is available to discuss these results and residual risks in detail.

REFERENCES
1. ACOG Committee Opinion No. 691: Carrier Screening for Genetic Conditions. Obstet Gynecol. 2017;129(3):e41-e55.
2. Watson MS, et al. Cystic fibrosis population carrier screening: 2004 revision of American College of Medical Genetics mutation panel. Genet Med. 2004;6(5):387-391.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director
